surfaces.part: backrest rear face with horizontal stripes

answer.evidence: Seen from behind, the main body is the backrest. Row 11 is the outline. Rows 12-15 are a lighter band across the whole width (L 157/123/123/157), with a bright edge line at row 15. Row 16 is a very dark shadow line (L=35). Rows 17-25 are the darker rear face, 9 rows, with horizontal stripes and seam columns. Row 26 is the bottom outline. The arms at the sides rise above the back (rows 8-10 are only 8 px wide) and have lighter caps. The seat cushion is hidden behind the backrest, which is expected from this angle. The top band is only 4 rows, but it does end in an edge line plus shadow, so it counts as a top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a blue sofa seen from behind with only 7 distinct colours in total, against 11-40 for the references. Its per-tile median is 5, well below the hedge (10), stall (17) and well (20). The back cushion has about 3 blue steps (light top band, mid blue, darker lower band) plus a dark blue-navy edge, where Beodeul materials carry 5-6 steps. The outline is a tinted dark blue (0% neutral dark edge pixels), so it is material-toned and not a black sticker line. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, but only because the surfaces are broken into a few smooth horizontal bands. There is no visible grain, stitching, fabric speckle or per-cushion highlight, so the texture reads as flat and clean-vector. The arms and legs are simple blocks with little form variation. Next to the hedge, stall and well it looks thinner and flatter, with much lower information density, so it fails.
